threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Finding it odd that the barista at the local café knows everyone's name except yours. It's like being in a sitcom where you’re the new character.
Caught the 381 last night, and a guy was trying to impress a girl by reciting Shakespeare. She rolled her eyes and got off at the next stop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last week, I saw a pigeon casually stealing a piece of vegan cake from a café table. Only in Neukölln would dessert banditry feel so normal.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find currywurst served with a side of techno beats at a late-night food stall. It's a wild mix of flavors and vibes!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they order a burrito with extra salsa, but leave the guac off because 'that's for tourists.'

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 at Civic Center today—guy in a Hawaiian shirt was jamming on a ukulele while waiting for the bus. Just another day in the city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can only find authentic tapas in the busy places. The best ones hide behind the locals’ smiles, in those tiny bars where the floor sticks to your shoes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the metro maps – constantly staring at their phones, while locals glide on without a glance.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think bus times are *suggestions*, not a lifestyle choice. Buses here are more like rare Pokémon—always just out of reach.
Caught the 333 last night, a guy was loudly explaining to a pigeon why he'd never date a cat. Bus driver didn't even blink.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I spotted a group of elderly men in the park, arguing passionately about the best kebab in town while sharing tea. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM while listening to live street performances. The blend of flavors and sounds is unparalleled.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they can name the taco truck parked on 24th that’s been there longer than most of the new cafes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week I watched a guy try to board the 19 Polk with a pet iguana on his shoulder. Muni riders just shrugged and let it happen.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the ‘Barcelona vibe’ is all beach and Gaudí. Try hearing the locals jamming in the plaça at midnight—pure magic that’s easily missed.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they struggle to understand the metro map—especially when they try to use their phones while moving.
